Eka raises $150 million to develop robots that learn from vision and force

Its vision-force-action approach targets adaptable manipulation; a reported 1,500 picks per hour still needs sustained production validation.

Humanoids Daily ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Funding for models and deployments

Eka Robotics announced a $150 million Series A on October 20, led by Andreessen Horowitz and F-Prime, to develop its model and customer deployments. Its founders are MIT researcher Pulkit Agrawal and former DeepMind researcher Tuomas Haarnoja, a co-creator of Soft Actor-Critic.

Contact becomes control feedback

The vision-force-action approach combines images with forces arising during contact. That feedback can help adjust a slipping grasp or correct alignment when insertion encounters resistance. Eka uses reinforcement learning in simulations with varied objects and contact conditions to train skills for physical hardware.

Laboratory speed is one part of readiness

Eka reports 1,500 picks per hour, with its investor describing laboratory testing. This does not establish full-shift factory readiness. Industrial evaluation also needs success rates, intervention requirements and performance across varied parts, beyond the speed of a demonstration.
